source.text: אֵיכָ֣ה׀יָשְׁבָ֣ה בָדָ֗ד הָעִיר֙ רַבָּ֣תִי עָ֔ם הָיְתָ֖ה כְּאַלְמָנָ֑ה רַּבָּ֣תִיבַגּוֹיִ֗ם שָׂרָ֨תִי֙ בַּמְּדִינ֔וֹת הָיְתָ֖ה לָמַֽס׃ס

records.literal_gloss: How sits alone the city great of people! She has become like a widow, great among [the] nations; princess among [the] provinces, she has become forced labor.

en.L: How she sits alone, the city [once] great with people! \q She has become like a widow, \q she [who was] great among the nations; \q [the] princess among the provinces has become a forced laborer.
en.B: How the city sits alone that once was crowded with people! \q She has become like a widow, \q she who was great among the nations; \q the princess of the provinces is now put to forced labor.
en.R: How lonely the city is now, the city that was once full of people! \q Now she is like a widow, \q though she was great among the nations. \q She was a princess over other lands, but now she must do forced labor.

pt.L: Como está sentada sozinha a cidade [antes] grande em povo! \q Tornou-se como uma viúva, \q ela [que era] grande entre as nações; \q a princesa entre as províncias tornou-se [sujeita a] trabalho forçado.
pt.B: Como está sozinha a cidade que antes fervilhava de gente! \q Ficou como uma viúva, \q ela que era grande entre as nações; \q a princesa das províncias agora é obrigada a trabalhos forçados.
pt.R: Como a cidade está solitária agora, ela que antes era cheia de gente! \q Agora está como uma viúva, \q embora fosse grande entre as nações. \q Ela era uma princesa sobre outras terras, mas agora tem de fazer trabalhos forçados.

es.L: ¡Cómo está sentada sola la ciudad [antes] llena de gente! \q Ha llegado a ser como una viuda, \q la [que era] grande entre las naciones; \q la princesa entre las provincias ha quedado sometida a trabajos forzados.
es.B: ¡Cómo se ha quedado sola la ciudad que antes rebosaba de gente! \q Se ha vuelto como una viuda, \q ella, que era grande entre las naciones; \q la princesa de las provincias está ahora sometida a trabajos forzados.
es.R: ¡Cómo se ha quedado sola la ciudad que antes estaba llena de gente! \q Ahora es como una viuda, \q aunque era grande entre las naciones. \q Era como una princesa sobre otras tierras, pero ahora tiene que hacer trabajos forzados.

vi.L: Than ôi! Nàng ngồi cô độc, thành [từng] đông dân! \q Nàng đã trở nên như người góa bụa, \q nàng [từng] cao trọng giữa các dân tộc; \q [bà] công chúa giữa các tỉnh đã trở thành kẻ làm lao dịch.
vi.B: Than ôi! Thành xưa kia đông đúc dân cư, nay ngồi trơ trọi một mình! \q Nàng đã trở nên như người góa bụa, \q nàng vốn cao trọng giữa các dân tộc; \q nàng là công chúa của các miền, nay phải chịu lao dịch.
vi.R: Than ôi! Thành này xưa kia đầy người, nay vắng vẻ cô đơn! \q Giờ đây nàng như một góa phụ, \q dù nàng từng lớn mạnh giữa các dân tộc. \q Nàng từng là công chúa trên các xứ khác, nhưng nay bị bắt làm lao dịch.

fr.L: Comme elle est assise solitaire, la ville [autrefois] grande en peuple ! \q Elle est devenue comme une veuve, \q elle [qui était] grande parmi les nations ; \q la princesse parmi les provinces est devenue corvéable.
fr.B: Comme elle est assise à l’écart, la ville qui était autrefois pleine de monde ! \q Elle est devenue comme une veuve, \q elle qui était grande parmi les nations ; \q la princesse des provinces est maintenant soumise aux travaux forcés.
fr.R: Comme elle est seule maintenant, la ville qui était autrefois pleine de monde ! \q Elle est maintenant comme une veuve, \q alors qu’elle était grande parmi les nations. \q Elle était comme une princesse au-dessus des autres pays, mais maintenant elle doit faire des travaux forcés.

sw.L: Jinsi mji uliokuwa mkuu kwa watu unavyokaa peke yake! \q Umekuwa kama mjane, \q [mji] uliokuwa mkuu kati ya mataifa; \q binti mfalme kati ya majimbo amekuwa mtumwa wa kazi za kulazimishwa.
sw.B: Jinsi mji uliokuwa umejaa watu unavyokaa peke yake! \q Umekuwa kama mjane, \q mji uliokuwa mkuu kati ya mataifa; \q binti mfalme wa majimbo sasa amelazimishwa kufanya kazi ya utumwa.
sw.R: Jinsi mji ulivyo mpweke sasa, mji ambao zamani ulijaa watu! \q Sasa ni kama mjane, \q ingawa ulikuwa mkuu kati ya mataifa. \q Ulikuwa kama binti mfalme juu ya nchi nyingine, lakini sasa unalazimishwa kufanya kazi ngumu.

ko.L: 어찌하여 홀로 앉아 있는가, [한때] 백성이 많던 그 성이! \q 과부처럼 되었다, \q 민족들 가운데 크던 그 성이. \q 지방들 가운데 공주였던 [그 성이] 강제 노역을 하는 자가 되었다.
ko.B: 어찌하여 이토록 쓸쓸히 앉아 있는가, 한때 사람들로 붐비던 그 성이! \q 과부와 같이 되었다, \q 뭇 민족 가운데 크던 그 성이. \q 여러 지방의 공주였던 성이 이제는 강제 노역에 끌려가는 신세가 되었다.
ko.R: 슬프다! 한때 사람들로 가득하던 성이 이제는 홀로 쓸쓸하게 앉아 있다. \q 그 성은 이제 과부와 같다. \q 한때는 여러 민족 가운데 으뜸이었는데도 그렇다. \q 다른 나라들 위에 공주 같던 성이 이제는 강제로 일을 해야 한다.

decisions.choice: an alphabet poem: twenty-two verses, one for each letter
decisions.reason: This chapter is an acrostic. Each of its twenty-two verses begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet in order: this verse with aleph, verse 2 with beth, and so on to taw in verse 22. Chapters 2 and 4 follow the same plan, chapter 3 gives each letter three verses, and chapter 5 has twenty-two verses but does not follow the alphabet. The form gives grief an order and a fullness, from the first letter to the last.

decisions.choice: How ...!: a cry of grief and shock, and the book's Hebrew title
decisions.reason: The word ('ekhah) is an exclamation, not a question: the cry of a mourner over the dead (compare Isaiah 1:21; Jeremiah 48:17), here over a fallen city. It opens chapters 1, 2 and 4, and it is the Hebrew name of the book.

decisions.choice: the lament rhythm: verses of three lines, each line long then short
decisions.reason: Most verses of this chapter have three lines (verse 7 has four). Many lines fall into a longer and a shorter half, a limping beat that was used for funeral songs (qinah, 2 Samuel 1:17; Amos 5:1-2). The Hebrew accents divide each verse in two, and the lines here follow those divisions.

decisions.choice: like a widow: bereft of husband and protector
decisions.reason: A widow had lost the one who provided for her and spoke for her, and she was easily wronged (Exodus 22:21; Isaiah 54:4). The city that was full of people now sits alone, emptied of her people and her king. The word "like" keeps it a picture: the city is not said to have lost her God for good.

decisions.choice: forced labor: work exacted by a ruling power
decisions.reason: The word (mas) names the labor gangs a ruler imposed on a subject people. Israel once put the Canaanites to such labor (Joshua 16:10; 1 Kings 9:21); now the princess among the provinces is the one made to serve. The reversal runs through the chapter.

decisions.choice: How ...!
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "How" with an exclamation mark, since the word is a cry, not a request for information, and it is the name of the book (m2). Chapters 2 and 4 open the same way.

decisions.choice: lonely ... now ... though ... over other lands
decisions.reason: Readable makes the contrast between then and now plain with "now" and "though", and says "other lands" for the provinces, the districts of an empire.

decisions.choice: Como ...! (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the mourner's cry that opens chapters 1, 2 and 4 (m2) is "Como ...!" with an exclamation mark, the Portuguese exclamation of grief and amazement, as the English keeps "How ...!". "Ai" is kept for the prophets' cry hoy (Isaiah, Jeremiah), a different word.

decisions.choice: trabalho forçado (L); trabalhos forçados (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word names the labor gangs imposed by a ruling power (m5), which Portuguese calls "trabalhos forçados"; "tributária" would mean paying tribute, a different burden.

decisions.choice: "¡Cómo ...!" as an exclamation
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word ('ekhah) is a mourner's cry, not a question, so every level writes it as an exclamation with ¡ ... !, as here and again in 2:1 and 4:1. It is the book's Hebrew title.

decisions.choice: the alphabet poem is not imitated; three lines per verse
decisions.reason: As in English, no level imitates the acrostic in Spanish: the verses cannot begin with the letters of the alphabet in order without forcing the sense. Each verse is set in lines (\q) at every level, at Spanish phrase boundaries, following the Hebrew's divisions (mostly three lines, the lament rhythm).

decisions.choice: "Than ôi!" for "ʾekah" ("How ...!") at every level, followed by the exclamation, here and in 2:1 and 4:1
decisions.reason: The word is a cry of grief, not a question, and it is the book's Hebrew title; "Than ôi" is the published Balanced wording of the same word in Isaiah 1:21. One wording at every level keeps the title word recognisable at the head of chapters 1, 2 and 4. Recorded once for the book.

decisions.choice: The alphabetic order of the verses is not reproduced; each English line break has one in Vietnamese at the same level
alternatives: Starting each verse with the letters of the Vietnamese alphabet
decisions.reason: Vietnamese cannot keep the Hebrew letter order without forcing the sense, so the lines follow the meaning and the meaning decisions name the acrostic. A verse is usually three lines, each keeping the long and short halves of the lament rhythm together. Recorded once for the book.

decisions.choice: Zion and the city are "nàng" ("she") in the third person at every level
decisions.reason: The poem pictures the city as a woman, a widow and a princess; "nàng" keeps that picture, as Jeremiah 4:31 does. Readable may say "thành" or "Si-ôn" where the English names her. Recorded once for the book.

decisions.choice: the exclamative "Comme … !" for "How …!" (ʾekhah), here and at 2:1 and 4:1
decisions.reason: The word is the book’s Hebrew title and a cry of grief, not a question. Modern French "Comment" reads as a question, so French uses the exclamative "Comme" at every level.

decisions.choice: present, passé composé and imparfait at every level, for the whole book; no passé simple
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Lamentations is speech: the poet, Zion and the man of chapter 3 speak. French speech uses the passé composé for the past, as the oracles of the prophets and the Psalms do, so all three levels use it here; the speakers’ words take no quotation marks, as in the English.

decisions.choice: "Jinsi ...!" with a -vyo- verb ("Jinsi mji ... unavyokaa peke yake!")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew 'ekhah opens chapters 1, 2 and 4 as a cry of grief and gives the book its Hebrew title (in Swahili the book is "Maombolezo"). Swahili's exclamative "Jinsi ...!" with a -vyo- verb keeps it an exclamation at every level rather than a question or a woe-cry; the same opening is used in 2:1 and 4:1.

decisions.choice: city agreement ("mji ... umekuwa") where the city is named; personal agreement ("binti mfalme ... amekuwa", "Sayuni ... naye", "Yerusalemu anakumbuka") where she is pictured as a woman
decisions.reason: Lamentations pictures Jerusalem and Zion as a widow, a princess and a mourning woman. Swahili verbs agree with the noun class, so the city noun "mji" takes u- forms, while Zion, Jerusalem and Judah personified take the personal a-/m- forms, as names for persons do. This holds through the book.

decisions.choice: "어찌하여 ... 가!" (Literal, Balanced); "슬프다!" followed by a plain sentence (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book's Hebrew title, 'ekhah, a cry of grief and shock (1:1; 2:1; 4:1). Literal and Balanced keep it as an exclamatory question; Readable opens with the lament cry "슬프다!", as Korean Isaiah 1:21 does for the same word, and then says the fact plainly. The same wording at each level returns in 2:1 and 4:1.

decisions.choice: the city is "그 성", never "그녀"
decisions.reason: Lamentations speaks of Zion and Jerusalem as a woman. Korean Bibles and the published Isaiah and Jeremiah never use "그녀" for her; this book repeats "그 성", "시온" or "예루살렘", or leaves the subject unsaid, and Readable's "시온 백성" takes "그들". Korean has no acrostic either: each verse keeps its own content, as the alphabet requires.

source.text: בָּכ֨וֹ תִבְכֶּ֜ה בַּלַּ֗יְלָה וְדִמְעָתָהּ֙ עַ֣ל לֶֽחֱיָ֔הּ אֵֽין־לָ֥הּ מְנַחֵ֖ם מִכָּל־אֹהֲבֶ֑יהָ כָּל־רֵעֶ֨יהָ֙ בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔הּ הָ֥יוּ לָ֖הּ לְאֹיְבִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Weeping she weeps in the night, and her tear[s] [are] on her cheek; there is not for her a comforter from all her lovers; all her friends have dealt treacherously with her, they have become to her enemies.

en.L: She weeps and weeps in the night, and her tears [are] on her cheek; \q she has no comforter among all her lovers; \q all her friends have dealt treacherously with her; they have become her enemies.
en.B: Bitterly she weeps through the night, with tears on her cheeks; \q of all her lovers there is not one to comfort her; \q all her friends have betrayed her and turned into her enemies.
en.R: She cries and cries all night long, with tears running down her face. \q She had many lovers, but none of them comforts her now. \q All her friends have turned against her and become her enemies.

pt.L: Ela chora e chora durante a noite, e as suas lágrimas [estão] na sua face; \q não tem quem a console entre todos os seus amantes; \q todos os seus amigos agiram com traição contra ela; tornaram-se seus inimigos.
pt.B: Amargamente ela chora pela noite afora, com lágrimas no rosto; \q de todos os seus amantes, nenhum está ali para consolá-la; \q todos os seus amigos a traíram e se tornaram seus inimigos.
pt.R: Ela chora e chora a noite inteira, com as lágrimas descendo pelo rosto. \q Ela tinha muitos amantes, mas agora nenhum deles a consola. \q Todos os seus amigos se voltaram contra ela e viraram seus inimigos.

es.L: Llora y llora de noche, y tiene las lágrimas en la mejilla; \q no tiene quien la consuele entre todos sus amantes; \q todos sus amigos la han traicionado; se le han vuelto enemigos.
es.B: Pasa la noche llorando con amargura, con lágrimas en las mejillas; \q de todos sus amantes no hay uno que la consuele; \q todos sus amigos la traicionaron y se volvieron sus enemigos.
es.R: Llora y llora toda la noche, y las lágrimas le corren por la cara. \q Tuvo muchos amantes, pero ahora ninguno la consuela. \q Todos sus amigos se pusieron en su contra y se convirtieron en sus enemigos.

vi.L: Nàng khóc, khóc mãi trong đêm, và nước mắt nàng [ở] trên má; \q giữa tất cả các người tình của nàng, nàng chẳng có ai an ủi; \q mọi bạn bè nàng đều đã phản bội nàng; chúng đã trở thành kẻ thù của nàng.
vi.B: Suốt đêm nàng khóc than cay đắng, nước mắt đẫm đôi má; \q trong tất cả các người tình của nàng, chẳng một ai an ủi nàng; \q bạn bè nàng thảy đều phản bội nàng và trở thành kẻ thù của nàng.
vi.R: Nàng khóc mãi suốt đêm, nước mắt chảy dài trên mặt. \q Nàng từng có nhiều người tình, nhưng nay chẳng ai an ủi nàng. \q Mọi bạn bè đều quay lưng lại với nàng và trở thành kẻ thù của nàng.

fr.L: Elle pleure, elle pleure dans la nuit, et ses larmes [sont] sur sa joue ; \q elle n’a pas de consolateur parmi tous ses amants ; \q tous ses amis ont agi perfidement envers elle ; ils sont devenus pour elle des ennemis.
fr.B: Elle pleure amèrement toute la nuit, les larmes sur les joues ; \q de tous ses amants, pas un seul ne la console ; \q tous ses amis l’ont trahie et sont devenus ses ennemis.
fr.R: Elle pleure et pleure toute la nuit, les larmes coulent sur son visage. \q Elle avait beaucoup d’amants, mais aucun ne la console maintenant. \q Tous ses amis se sont retournés contre elle et sont devenus ses ennemis.

sw.L: Analia na kulia usiku, na machozi yake [yako] shavuni mwake; \q hana mfariji kati ya wapenzi wake wote; \q rafiki zake wote wamemtendea hila; wamekuwa adui zake.
sw.B: Analia kwa uchungu usiku kucha, machozi yakitiririka mashavuni mwake; \q kati ya wapenzi wake wote hakuna hata mmoja wa kumfariji; \q rafiki zake wote wamemsaliti na kugeuka kuwa adui zake.
sw.R: Analia na kulia usiku wote, machozi yakimtiririka usoni. \q Alikuwa na wapenzi wengi, lakini hakuna hata mmoja anayemfariji sasa. \q Rafiki zake wote wamemgeuka, wamekuwa adui zake.

ko.L: 밤에 울고 또 우니, 눈물이 뺨에 [흐른다]. \q 그 성의 모든 연인 가운데 위로하는 자가 없다. \q 그 성의 친구들이 모두 그 성을 배신하여 원수가 되었다.
ko.B: 밤새도록 서럽게 우니, 두 뺨에 눈물이 흘러내린다. \q 사랑하던 이들 가운데 그 성을 위로할 이가 하나도 없다. \q 친구들은 모두 그 성을 배신하고 원수로 돌아섰다.
ko.R: 그 성은 밤새도록 울고 또 운다. 눈물이 얼굴을 타고 흘러내린다. \q 그 성을 사랑하던 이들이 많았지만, 이제는 아무도 위로해 주지 않는다. \q 친구들도 모두 등을 돌려 원수가 되었다.

decisions.choice: weeping she weeps: she weeps without stopping
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled, a Hebrew way of making it strong: she weeps hard and long. "In the night" adds that her grief gives her no rest when others sleep.

decisions.choice: her lovers, her friends: the nations she trusted as allies
decisions.reason: The city is pictured as a woman who turned from her husband to lovers. The prophets use this picture for Judah's alliances with other nations and the trust she put in them and in their gods (Jeremiah 4:30; 22:20-22; 30:14). Those allies did nothing for her, and some joined her enemies.

decisions.choice: comforter: one who comes to console a mourner
decisions.reason: A comforter was the friend or relative who came to sit with someone in grief (Genesis 37:35; Job 2:11). "No one to comfort her" returns again and again in this chapter (verses 9, 16, 17, 21).

decisions.choice: Bitterly she weeps (Balanced); She cries and cries (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the force of the doubled verb with "bitterly", Readable by repeating the verb (m1).

decisions.choice: não tem quem a console; nenhum ... para consolá-la (a verb, not a noun)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the refrain of the comforter (m3) is said with the verb "consolar" ("quem a console", "ninguém que me console"), as Portuguese naturally says it. The noun "consolador" is rare in speech and makes Portuguese readers think of the Spirit, "o Consolador" of John 14.

decisions.choice: "các người tình" for "her lovers"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew keeps the picture of an unfaithful woman whose lovers have left her; the meaning decision says they are the allied nations, so the word is kept at every level and Readable names the nations only where the English does (1:19).

source.text: גָּֽלְתָ֨ה יְהוּדָ֤ה מֵעֹ֨נִי֙ וּמֵרֹ֣ב עֲבֹדָ֔ה הִ֚יא יָשְׁבָ֣ה בַגּוֹיִ֔ם לֹ֥א מָצְאָ֖ה מָנ֑וֹחַ כָּל־רֹדְפֶ֥יהָ הִשִּׂיג֖וּהָ בֵּ֥ין הַמְּצָרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Has gone into exile Judah from affliction and from greatness of servitude; she dwells among the nations, not she has found a resting place; all her pursuers have overtaken her between the narrow places.

en.L: Judah has gone into exile from affliction and from great servitude; \q she dwells among the nations, she has found no resting place; \q all her pursuers have overtaken her between the narrow places.
en.B: Judah has gone into exile after misery and hard servitude; \q she lives among the nations and finds no place to rest; \q all who chased her have caught her in the narrow passes.
en.R: Judah has been taken away into exile after suffering and cruel, hard work. \q She lives among the nations and finds no place to rest. \q Everyone who chased her has caught her where she could not escape.

pt.L: Judá foi para o exílio depois de aflição e de grande servidão; \q ela habita entre as nações, não encontrou lugar de repouso; \q todos os seus perseguidores a alcançaram entre os lugares estreitos.
pt.B: Judá foi para o exílio depois de miséria e de dura servidão; \q vive entre as nações e não encontra lugar para descansar; \q todos os que a perseguiam a alcançaram nos desfiladeiros.
pt.R: Judá partiu para o exílio depois de muito sofrimento e de trabalhos duros e cruéis. \q Ela vive entre as nações e não encontra lugar para descansar. \q Todos os que a perseguiam a alcançaram num lugar de onde ela não podia escapar.

es.L: Judá ha ido al destierro después de la aflicción y de la mucha servidumbre; \q ella habita entre las naciones, no ha hallado lugar de descanso; \q todos sus perseguidores la han alcanzado entre los lugares estrechos.
es.B: Judá ha marchado al destierro después de la miseria y de una dura servidumbre; \q vive entre las naciones y no encuentra dónde descansar; \q todos los que la perseguían la alcanzaron en los desfiladeros.
es.R: Judá fue llevada al destierro después de mucho sufrimiento y de trabajos duros y crueles. \q Vive entre las naciones y no encuentra un lugar para descansar. \q Todos los que la perseguían la atraparon donde no podía escapar.

vi.L: Giu-đa đã đi lưu đày sau cơn khốn khổ và sau lao dịch nặng nề; \q nàng ở giữa các dân tộc, nàng không tìm được chỗ nghỉ ngơi; \q mọi kẻ đuổi theo nàng đã bắt kịp nàng giữa những chỗ hẹp.
vi.B: Giu-đa đã bị lưu đày sau bao khốn khổ và cảnh tôi đòi cực nhọc; \q nàng sống giữa các dân tộc mà chẳng tìm được nơi an nghỉ; \q mọi kẻ săn đuổi đã bắt được nàng nơi những khe hẹp.
vi.R: Dân Giu-đa đã bị bắt đi lưu đày sau bao đau khổ và lao động cực nhọc, tàn ác. \q Nàng sống giữa các dân tộc và không tìm được chỗ nghỉ ngơi. \q Mọi kẻ đuổi theo đã bắt được nàng ở nơi nàng không thể thoát.

fr.L: Juda est partie en exil après l’affliction et après une grande servitude ; \q elle habite parmi les nations, elle n’a pas trouvé de lieu de repos ; \q tous ses poursuivants l’ont atteinte entre les passages étroits.
fr.B: Juda est partie en exil après la misère et une dure servitude ; \q elle vit parmi les nations et ne trouve pas où se reposer ; \q tous ceux qui la poursuivaient l’ont rattrapée dans les défilés.
fr.R: Juda a été emmenée en exil après avoir souffert et subi un travail dur et cruel. \q Elle vit parmi les nations et ne trouve aucun endroit pour se reposer. \q Tous ceux qui la poursuivaient l’ont rattrapée là où elle ne pouvait pas s’échapper.

sw.L: Yuda amekwenda uhamishoni kutoka mateso na kutoka utumwa mwingi; \q anakaa kati ya mataifa, hajapata mahali pa kupumzika; \q wote wanaomfuatia wamempata katikati ya mahali pembamba.
sw.B: Yuda amekwenda uhamishoni baada ya taabu na utumwa mzito; \q anaishi kati ya mataifa wala hapati mahali pa kupumzika; \q wote waliomwinda wamemkamata katika njia nyembamba.
sw.R: Yuda amechukuliwa uhamishoni baada ya kuteseka na kufanya kazi ngumu ya kikatili. \q Anaishi kati ya mataifa wala hapati mahali pa kupumzika. \q Wote waliomfukuza wamemkamata mahali ambapo hawezi kutoroka.

ko.L: 유다가 고난과 많은 노역을 [겪은] 뒤에 포로로 끌려갔다. \q 민족들 가운데 살면서 쉴 곳을 찾지 못한다. \q 뒤쫓는 자들이 모두 좁은 곳들 사이에서 유다를 따라잡았다.
ko.B: 유다는 고난과 혹독한 종살이 끝에 포로로 끌려갔다. \q 뭇 민족 가운데 살면서 쉴 곳을 얻지 못한다. \q 뒤쫓는 자들이 모두 좁은 길목에서 유다를 붙잡았다.
ko.R: 유다는 고생하고 힘든 일에 시달리다가 포로로 끌려갔다. \q 다른 민족들 사이에서 살지만 쉴 곳을 찾지 못한다. \q 뒤쫓는 사람들이 모두 피할 길이 없는 곳에서 유다를 붙잡았다.

decisions.choice: from affliction: after a time of suffering and servitude
decisions.reason: The small word "from" can mean "after" or "because of". Read as "after", Judah's exile came on top of years of suffering under foreign powers. Read as "because of", some of Judah's people left the land to escape that suffering. The first fits the chapter, where exile is the last of her losses.

decisions.choice: she has found no resting place: the curse of Deuteronomy come true
decisions.reason: Moses warned that if Israel broke the covenant, "among those nations you will find no rest, no resting place for the sole of your foot" (Deuteronomy 28:64-65). The same word for a resting place is used there.

decisions.choice: between the narrow places: trapped with no way out
decisions.reason: The word is used of a narrow pass between rocks, a place where those being chased are caught. It also stands for distress in general (Psalm 116:3). Judah was overtaken like someone run down in a ravine. Judah's king was caught as he fled (2 Kings 25:4-5).

decisions.choice: where she could not escape
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the narrow places (m3).

decisions.choice: depois de (every level)
decisions.reason: Portuguese "da aflição" after "foi para o exílio" would read only as the place she left, and Portuguese has no small word with both senses of the Hebrew. Every level follows the reading m1 prefers, "after".

decisions.choice: Judah in the feminine: "ella", "llevada"
decisions.reason: Judah is pictured as a woman, as Zion and Jerusalem are, so Spanish keeps the feminine agreement (ella, la, llevada) that the Hebrew has.

decisions.choice: "Juda est partie", "elle": Judah with feminine agreement
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pictures Judah as a woman (the verbs and pronouns are feminine), as it does Zion and Jerusalem throughout the book; French keeps the feminine agreement at every level rather than the usual masculine of the name.

source.text: דַּרְכֵ֨י צִיּ֜וֹן אֲבֵל֗וֹת מִבְּלִי֙ בָּאֵ֣י מוֹעֵ֔ד כָּל־שְׁעָרֶ֨יהָ֙ שֽׁוֹמֵמִ֔ין כֹּהֲנֶ֖יהָ נֶאֱנָחִ֑ים בְּתוּלֹתֶ֥יהָ נּוּג֖וֹתוְהִ֥יא מַר־לָֽהּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] roads of Zion [are] mourning from no ones coming [to the] appointed feast; all her gates [are] desolate, her priests [are] groaning; her virgins [are] grieved, and she, bitter to her.

en.L: The roads of Zion mourn, because none come to the appointed feast; \q all her gates are desolate, her priests groan; \q her virgins are grieved, and as for her, [it is] bitter to her.
en.B: The roads to Zion mourn, for no one comes to the festivals; \q all her gates are deserted, her priests groan; \q her young women grieve, and she herself is in bitter pain.
en.R: The roads to Zion are sad and empty, because no one comes to the festivals anymore. \q All her city gates are deserted, and her priests groan. \q Her young women are full of sorrow, and Zion herself is in bitter pain.

pt.L: Os caminhos de Sião estão de luto, porque ninguém vem à festa marcada; \q todas as suas portas estão desoladas, os seus sacerdotes gemem; \q as suas virgens estão aflitas, e quanto a ela, [é] amargo para ela.
pt.B: Os caminhos que levam a Sião estão de luto, pois ninguém vem às festas; \q todas as suas portas estão desertas, os seus sacerdotes gemem; \q as suas moças sofrem, e ela mesma está numa dor amarga.
pt.R: Os caminhos que levam a Sião estão tristes e vazios, porque ninguém mais vem para as festas. \q Todas as portas da cidade estão desertas, e os seus sacerdotes gemem. \q As suas moças estão cheias de tristeza, e a própria Sião sofre uma dor amarga.

es.L: Los caminos de Sion están de luto, porque nadie viene a la fiesta señalada; \q todas sus puertas están desoladas, sus sacerdotes gimen; \q sus vírgenes están afligidas, y ella misma [vive en] amargura.
es.B: Los caminos que llevan a Sion están de luto, porque nadie acude a las fiestas; \q todas sus puertas están desiertas, sus sacerdotes gimen; \q sus muchachas están afligidas, y ella sufre con amargura.
es.R: Los caminos que llevan a Sion están tristes y vacíos, porque ya nadie viene a las fiestas. \q Todas las puertas de la ciudad están desiertas, y sus sacerdotes gimen. \q Sus muchachas están llenas de tristeza, y Sion misma sufre un dolor amargo.

vi.L: Các con đường của Si-ôn than khóc, vì chẳng ai đến dự kỳ lễ đã định; \q mọi cổng thành nàng đều hoang vắng, các thầy tế lễ của nàng rên siết; \q các trinh nữ của nàng sầu muộn, còn nàng, [thật] cay đắng cho nàng.
vi.B: Các nẻo đường lên Si-ôn than khóc, vì không ai còn đến dự các kỳ lễ; \q mọi cổng thành nàng vắng tanh, các thầy tế lễ nàng rên rỉ; \q các thiếu nữ nàng buồn rầu, và chính nàng đau đớn cay đắng.
vi.R: Những con đường lên Si-ôn buồn bã và vắng vẻ, vì không còn ai đến dự các kỳ lễ nữa. \q Mọi cổng thành đều vắng tanh, và các thầy tế lễ rên rỉ. \q Các thiếu nữ đầy sầu khổ, và chính Si-ôn cũng đau đớn cay đắng.

fr.L: Les chemins de Sion sont en deuil, parce que personne ne vient à la fête fixée ; \q toutes ses portes sont désolées, ses prêtres gémissent ; \q ses vierges sont affligées, et quant à elle, [c’est] amer pour elle.
fr.B: Les routes qui mènent à Sion sont en deuil, car personne ne vient plus aux fêtes ; \q toutes ses portes sont désertes, ses prêtres gémissent ; \q ses jeunes filles sont dans la peine, et elle-même souffre amèrement.
fr.R: Les routes qui mènent à Sion sont tristes et vides, parce que personne ne vient plus aux fêtes. \q Toutes les portes de la ville sont désertes, et ses prêtres gémissent. \q Ses jeunes filles sont pleines de chagrin, et Sion elle-même souffre amèrement.

sw.L: Njia za Sayuni zinaomboleza, kwa sababu hakuna wanaokuja kwenye sikukuu iliyoamriwa; \q malango yake yote ni ukiwa, makuhani wake wanaugua; \q mabikira wake wana huzuni, naye mwenyewe [ana] uchungu.
sw.B: Barabara za kwenda Sayuni zinaomboleza, kwa maana hakuna anayekuja kwenye sikukuu; \q malango yake yote yamebaki tupu, makuhani wake wanaugua; \q wasichana wake wanahuzunika, naye mwenyewe yuko katika uchungu mkali.
sw.R: Barabara za kwenda Sayuni zina huzuni na ziko tupu, kwa sababu hakuna anayekuja tena kwenye sikukuu. \q Malango yote ya mji hayana watu, na makuhani wake wanaugua. \q Wasichana wake wamejaa huzuni, na Sayuni mwenyewe yuko katika maumivu makali.

ko.L: 시온의 길들이 슬퍼한다. 정한 절기에 오는 자가 없기 때문이다. \q 그 성의 모든 성문이 황폐하고, 그 성의 제사장들이 탄식한다. \q 그 성의 처녀들이 근심하고, 그 성도 쓰라림 속에 있다.
ko.B: 시온으로 가는 길들이 슬퍼한다. 절기를 지키러 오는 사람이 없기 때문이다. \q 성문은 모두 황량하고, 제사장들은 탄식한다. \q 젊은 여자들은 근심에 잠겼고, 시온 자신도 쓰라린 고통 속에 있다.
ko.R: 시온으로 가는 길들이 텅 빈 채 슬퍼한다. 이제는 절기를 지키러 오는 사람이 아무도 없다. \q 성문은 모두 쓸쓸하고, 제사장들은 신음한다. \q 젊은 여자들은 슬픔에 잠겼고, 시온도 몹시 괴로워한다.

decisions.choice: the roads mourn: the empty roads are pictured as mourners
decisions.reason: The roads that once carried crowds of pilgrims lie empty. Like the land in the prophets (Isaiah 24:4; Jeremiah 12:4), they are said to mourn.

decisions.choice: the appointed feast: the yearly pilgrim festivals at the temple
decisions.reason: The word (mo'ed) means an appointed time and so a set festival. Three times a year the people came up to the LORD's house for the great feasts (Deuteronomy 16:16). With the temple burned, no one comes.

decisions.choice: her virgins: the city's young unmarried women
decisions.reason: The word means young women of marriageable age. They led the singing and dancing at festivals and weddings (Judges 21:19-21; Jeremiah 31:13), so their grief marks the end of every celebration.

decisions.choice: are grieved
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is from a root meaning to suffer grief. The ancient Greek translation reads "are led away", which may reflect a slightly different Hebrew word. The Hebrew reading is kept.

decisions.choice: young women
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "young women", which names the same people as the Literal "virgins" (m3).

decisions.choice: as moças
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Balanced and Readable say "as moças", the plain Brazilian word for young unmarried women (m3), where the English says "young women"; Literal keeps "as virgens".

decisions.choice: "sus muchachas"
decisions.reason: The word means the city's young unmarried women; Balanced and Readable use the plain everyday word, as the English has "young women". Literal keeps "vírgenes".

decisions.choice: "ses jeunes filles" for "her virgins" (Balanced, Readable), for the whole book; Literal "ses vierges"
decisions.reason: French "jeunes filles" carries the sense of young unmarried women (m3) that the English "young women" gives; "jeunes femmes" would suggest wives.

source.text: הָי֨וּ צָרֶ֤יהָ לְרֹאשׁ֙ אֹיְבֶ֣יהָ שָׁל֔וּ כִּֽי־יְהוָ֥ה הוֹגָ֖הּ עַ֣ל רֹב־פְּשָׁעֶ֑יהָ עוֹלָלֶ֛יהָ הָלְכ֥וּ שְׁבִ֖י לִפְנֵי־צָֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Have become her foes [the] head, her enemies are at ease, for Yahweh has grieved her on [account of the] multitude of her transgressions; her children have gone [into] captivity before [the] foe.

en.L: Her foes have become the head, her enemies are at ease, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has made her suffer for the multitude of her transgressions; \q her children have gone away captive before the foe.
en.B: Her foes have become her masters, her enemies live at ease, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought grief on her for her many rebellions; \q her little ones have gone into captivity ahead of the foe.
en.R: Her enemies now rule over her and live in comfort. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has made her suffer because she rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} so many times. \q Her children have been taken away as prisoners, driven ahead of the enemy.

pt.L: Os seus adversários tornaram-se a cabeça, os seus inimigos estão tranquilos, \q porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} a fez sofrer pela multidão das suas transgressões; \q as suas crianças foram para o cativeiro diante do adversário.
pt.B: Os seus adversários se tornaram os seus senhores, os seus inimigos vivem tranquilos, \q pois {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} trouxe aflição sobre ela por causa das suas muitas rebeldias; \q os seus pequeninos foram para o cativeiro à frente do adversário.
pt.R: Agora os inimigos dela mandam nela e vivem com conforto. \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} a fez sofrer porque ela se rebelou contra {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tantas vezes. \q As suas crianças foram levadas como prisioneiras, empurradas à frente do inimigo.

es.L: Sus adversarios han llegado a ser la cabeza, sus enemigos están tranquilos, \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} la ha afligido por la multitud de sus transgresiones; \q sus niños han ido en cautiverio delante del adversario.
es.B: Sus adversarios se han vuelto sus amos, sus enemigos viven tranquilos, \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} la ha hecho sufrir por sus muchos delitos; \q sus pequeños han ido al cautiverio delante del adversario.
es.R: Ahora sus enemigos la dominan y viven cómodos. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} la ha hecho sufrir porque pecó contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tantas veces. \q A sus niños se los llevaron prisioneros, empujándolos delante del enemigo.

vi.L: Các kẻ địch của nàng đã trở nên đầu, các kẻ thù của nàng được thảnh thơi, \q vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã làm nàng sầu khổ vì vô số tội vi phạm của nàng; \q các con nhỏ của nàng đã đi làm phu tù trước mặt kẻ địch.
vi.B: Quân địch nay làm chủ nàng, kẻ thù nàng sống an nhàn, \q vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giáng sầu khổ trên nàng bởi vô số tội phản nghịch của nàng; \q con trẻ nàng bị bắt làm phu tù, bị lùa đi trước quân địch.
vi.R: Nay kẻ thù cai trị nàng và sống sung sướng. \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã làm cho nàng đau khổ vì nàng đã phản nghịch {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} quá nhiều lần. \q Con cái nàng bị bắt làm tù binh, bị lùa đi trước mặt quân thù.

fr.L: Ses adversaires sont devenus la tête, ses ennemis sont tranquilles, \q car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a fait souffrir pour la multitude de ses transgressions ; \q ses petits enfants sont partis captifs devant l’adversaire.
fr.B: Ses adversaires sont devenus ses maîtres, ses ennemis vivent en paix, \q car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a accablée de chagrin pour ses nombreuses rébellions ; \q ses petits enfants sont partis en captivité devant l’adversaire.
fr.R: Ses ennemis la dominent maintenant et vivent à leur aise. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a fait souffrir parce qu’elle s’est révoltée tant de fois contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. \q Ses enfants ont été emmenés comme prisonniers, poussés devant l’ennemi.

sw.L: Watesi wake wamekuwa kichwa, adui zake wanastarehe, \q kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemhuzunisha kwa ajili ya wingi wa maasi yake; \q watoto wake wamekwenda utumwani mbele ya mtesi.
sw.B: Watesi wake wamekuwa mabwana zake, adui zake wanaishi kwa raha, \q kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemletea huzuni kwa ajili ya makosa yake mengi; \q watoto wake wadogo wamechukuliwa mateka, wakitangulizwa mbele ya mtesi.
sw.R: Adui zake sasa wanamtawala na kuishi kwa raha. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemtesa kwa sababu alitenda dhambi nyingi sana dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \q Watoto wake wamechukuliwa mateka, wakiswagwa mbele ya adui.

ko.L: 그 성의 대적들이 머리가 되었고, 그 성의 원수들이 평안하다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 성의 많은 반역 때문에 그 성을 괴롭게 하셨기 때문이다. \q 그 성의 어린 자녀들이 대적 앞에서 포로가 되어 끌려갔다.
ko.B: 대적들이 그 성의 주인이 되었고, 원수들은 편안히 지낸다. \q 그 성이 반역을 많이 저질렀으므로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 성에 슬픔을 안기셨다. \q 어린 자녀들은 포로가 되어 대적 앞에서 끌려갔다.
ko.R: 원수들이 이제 그 성을 다스리며 편안하게 산다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 성을 고통스럽게 하셨다. 그 성이 그분께 수없이 죄를 지었기 때문이다. \q 그 성의 아이들은 포로가 되어 원수들 앞에서 끌려갔다.

decisions.choice: her foes have become the head: the curse of Deuteronomy come true
decisions.reason: Moses promised that a faithful Israel would be "the head and not the tail", and warned that if they broke the covenant the foreigner would be the head and they the tail (Deuteronomy 28:13, 44).

decisions.choice: the LORD has made her suffer for her transgressions
decisions.reason: The poet does not see the disaster as chance or as the enemy's work alone. The LORD has brought it, and the cause is her many acts of rebellion against him (verses 8, 14, 18, 22). The word for transgression (pesha') means rebellion, the breaking of faith with a lord.

decisions.choice: her children before the foe: captives driven ahead of their captors
decisions.reason: Prisoners of war were marched in front of the conquering army. The word for children means little ones, too young to fight.

decisions.choice: masters (Balanced); rule over her (Readable); rebellions
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what being "the head" means here (m1), and they say "rebellions" or "rebelled" for the word Literal renders "transgressions" (m2).

decisions.choice: rebelled against him
decisions.reason: Readable names the one she rebelled against, the LORD.

decisions.choice: "transgresiones" (L), "delitos" (B), "pecó" (R)
decisions.reason: Kept the same through the book for pesha', as the Spanish prophets have it: Literal "transgresión", Balanced "delito", Readable "pecado" or "pecar". The English Balanced "rebellions" is carried by the verb "rebelarse" where the Hebrew has the verb (1:18, 20).

decisions.choice: "tội vi phạm" (Literal); "tội phản nghịch" (Balanced); "phản nghịch" or "tội lỗi" (Readable) for "peshaʿ"
decisions.reason: The word is rebellion against a master, which the English Balanced "rebellions" brings out; Literal keeps the general "tội vi phạm" of the prophets, and Readable says it plainly. Kept through the book (1:14, 22; 3:42).

decisions.choice: "transgressions" (L), "rébellions" (B), "péchés" or "se révolter" (R) for peshaʿ, for the whole book
decisions.reason: The prophets’ terms for peshaʿ, so that the book reads with Isaiah, Jeremiah and the Twelve; Balanced "rébellions" follows the English Balanced here.

decisions.choice: "maasi" (L), "makosa" (B), "dhambi" (R) for pesha'
decisions.reason: Pesha' is rebellion against a master. Literal keeps "maasi" (acts of rebellion), Balanced "makosa", the usual word for wrongs in a public reading, and Readable the everyday "dhambi", as in Psalm 51:3 and the prophets. The verb is "kuasi". The same split holds through the book.

decisions.choice: "반역" (Literal, Balanced); "죄를 짓다" (Readable) for pesha'
decisions.reason: The word for open rebellion against God, as in the prophets: "반역" at Literal and Balanced, the plain "죄" at Readable. The same wording holds through the book.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span; "그분" with -시-
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change. Where the English has a span, Korean carries the respect with "그분", "께서" and the honorific -시-, at every level and through the book.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֥א מִבַּת־צִיּ֖וֹן כָּל־הֲדָרָ֑הּ הָי֣וּ שָׂרֶ֗יהָ כְּאַיָּלִים֙ לֹא־מָצְא֣וּ מִרְעֶ֔ה וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ בְלֹא־כֹ֖חַ לִפְנֵ֥י רוֹדֵֽף׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And has gone out from [the] daughter of Zion all her splendor; her princes have become like deer [that] not have found pasture, and they have gone without strength before [the] pursuer.

en.L: And from the daughter of Zion all her splendor has departed; \q her princes have become like deer [that] find no pasture, \q and they have gone without strength before the pursuer.
en.B: All her splendor has gone from Daughter Zion; \q her officials are like deer that find no pasture; \q they stumble on without strength ahead of the hunter.
en.R: The people of Zion have lost all their splendor. \q Their leaders are like deer that cannot find any grass to eat. \q They are too weak to get away from the hunter.

pt.L: E saiu da filha de Sião todo o seu esplendor; \q os seus príncipes tornaram-se como cervos [que] não encontram pasto, \q e andaram sem força diante do perseguidor.
pt.B: Todo o esplendor se foi da filha de Sião; \q os seus oficiais são como cervos que não acham pasto; \q vão cambaleando, sem forças, à frente do caçador.
pt.R: O povo de Sião perdeu todo o seu esplendor. \q Os seus líderes são como cervos que não conseguem encontrar capim para comer. \q Estão fracos demais para fugir do caçador.

es.L: Y de la hija de Sion se ha ido todo su esplendor; \q sus príncipes han llegado a ser como ciervos [que] no hallan pasto, \q y han ido sin fuerzas delante del perseguidor.
es.B: Todo su esplendor se ha ido de la hija de Sion; \q sus jefes son como ciervos que no encuentran pasto; \q avanzan sin fuerzas delante del cazador.
es.R: El pueblo de Sion ha perdido todo su esplendor. \q Sus dirigentes son como ciervos que no encuentran hierba para comer. \q Están demasiado débiles para escapar del cazador.

vi.L: Và khỏi con gái Si-ôn mọi vẻ huy hoàng của nàng đã ra đi; \q các thủ lĩnh của nàng đã trở nên như những con nai không tìm được đồng cỏ, \q và họ đã đi mà không còn sức trước mặt kẻ đuổi theo.
vi.B: Mọi vẻ huy hoàng đã lìa khỏi con gái Si-ôn; \q các quan chức nàng như bầy nai chẳng tìm ra đồng cỏ; \q họ lê bước kiệt sức trước mặt kẻ săn đuổi.
vi.R: Dân Si-ôn đã mất hết vẻ huy hoàng. \q Các nhà lãnh đạo của họ như những con nai không tìm được cỏ để ăn. \q Họ quá yếu đuối, không thể chạy thoát khỏi kẻ săn đuổi.

fr.L: Et de la fille de Sion toute sa splendeur est partie ; \q ses chefs sont devenus comme des cerfs [qui] ne trouvent pas de pâture, \q et ils sont allés sans force devant le poursuivant.
fr.B: Toute sa splendeur a quitté la fille de Sion ; \q ses chefs sont comme des cerfs qui ne trouvent pas de pâturage ; \q ils avancent sans force devant le chasseur.
fr.R: Le peuple de Sion a perdu toute sa splendeur. \q Ses dirigeants sont comme des cerfs qui ne trouvent rien à brouter. \q Ils sont trop faibles pour échapper au chasseur.

sw.L: Na kutoka kwa binti Sayuni fahari yake yote imeondoka; \q wakuu wake wamekuwa kama ayala [ambao] hawapati malisho, \q nao wamekwenda bila nguvu mbele ya mfuatiaji.
sw.B: Fahari yake yote imemtoka Binti Sayuni; \q maafisa wake ni kama ayala wasiopata malisho; \q wanajikokota bila nguvu mbele ya mwindaji.
sw.R: Watu wa Sayuni wamepoteza fahari yao yote. \q Viongozi wao ni kama ayala wasioweza kupata majani ya kula. \q Wamechoka mno, hawawezi kumkimbia mwindaji.

ko.L: 딸 시온에게서 그 모든 영화가 떠나갔다. \q 그 성의 고관들은 꼴을 찾지 못한 사슴들 같이 되어, \q 쫓는 자 앞에서 힘없이 걸어갔다.
ko.B: 딸 시온에게서 그 모든 영화가 사라졌다. \q 그 성의 관리들은 풀밭을 찾지 못한 사슴들 같다. \q 그들은 사냥꾼에게 쫓기며 힘없이 비틀거리며 간다.
ko.R: 시온 백성은 그 모든 영광을 잃었다. \q 그들의 지도자들은 먹을 풀을 찾지 못한 사슴들 같다. \q 그들은 너무 약해서 사냥꾼에게서 달아나지 못한다.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Zion: Jerusalem and its people pictured as a young woman
decisions.reason: Zion is the hill of the temple and stands for Jerusalem. "Daughter Zion" pictures the city and its people as a young woman, loved and now shamed (2:1; Isaiah 1:8). The chapter speaks of the city as "she" throughout.

decisions.choice: deer: hunted animals weakened by hunger
decisions.reason: Starved deer cannot outrun the hunter. The ancient Greek translation reads "rams", which needs only different vowels in the Hebrew; the Hebrew reading fits the picture of flight.

decisions.choice: her princes ... before the pursuer: the flight of Judah's leaders
decisions.reason: When the Babylonians broke through the wall, King Zedekiah and his men fled by night and were overtaken near Jericho (2 Kings 25:4-6). The word for princes (sar) means the king's chief men.

decisions.choice: officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The king's chief men (sar) are "princes" at Literal, as in Isaiah and Jeremiah; Balanced and Readable say "officials" and "leaders", since they were not the king's sons.

decisions.choice: the people of Zion ... their
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Zion" for "the daughter of Zion", as Isaiah does, and so speaks of "their" splendor and leaders (m1).

decisions.choice: a filha de Sião (L, B); o povo de Sião (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as in Isaiah and Jeremiah: the city pictured as a young woman (m1) is "a filha de Sião" at Literal and Balanced, the natural Portuguese form; "Filha Sião", as the English Balanced says "Daughter Zion", is not Portuguese. Readable says "o povo de Sião", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "la hija de Sion" (L, B); "el pueblo de Sion" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah and Jeremiah in Spanish. Readable names the people, since the picture of the city as a daughter is not plain to new readers. The same pattern holds for "la hija de Jerusalén" / "la gente de Jerusalén" and "la hija de mi pueblo".

decisions.choice: "príncipes" (L), "jefes" (B), "dirigentes" (R)
decisions.reason: The leaders (sarim) take the words the Spanish prophets use for them.

decisions.choice: "con gái Si-ôn" (Literal, Balanced); "dân Si-ôn" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The form for "daughter Zion" used in Isaiah, Jeremiah and 2 Kings 19:21; kept through the book.

decisions.choice: "la fille de Sion" (L, B), "le peuple de Sion" (R), for the whole book; likewise "la fille de Juda", "la fille de Jérusalem"
decisions.reason: As published Isaiah and Jeremiah: French has no natural equivalent of the English Balanced "Daughter Zion", so Balanced keeps "la fille de Sion"; Readable names the people, except where Zion goes on speaking as a woman.

decisions.choice: "ses chefs" (L, B), "ses dirigeants" (R) for sarim, for the whole book
decisions.reason: The term chosen for sarim across the prophets; French "princes" would suggest the royal family.

decisions.choice: "binti Sayuni" (L), "Binti Sayuni" (B), "watu wa Sayuni" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah and Jeremiah: Literal keeps the figure as it stands, Balanced capitalizes it as a name for the city pictured as a young woman, and Readable says who is meant. "Binti Yerusalemu", "Binti Yuda" and "Binti Edomu" follow the same pattern in this book.

decisions.choice: "딸 시온" (Literal, Balanced); "시온 백성" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Daughter Zion as the published Korean Isaiah and Jeremiah word it (2 Kings 19:21 = Isaiah 37:22), at each level through the book. Readable's "시온 백성" takes "그들".

source.text: זָֽכְרָ֣ה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם יְמֵ֤י עָנְיָהּ֙ וּמְרוּדֶ֔יהָ כֹּ֚ל מַחֲמֻדֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ מִ֣ימֵי קֶ֑דֶם בִּנְפֹ֧ל עַמָּ֣הּ בְּיַד־צָ֗ר וְאֵ֤ין עוֹזֵר֙ לָ֔הּ רָא֣וּהָ צָרִ֔ים שָׂחֲק֖וּ עַ֥ל מִשְׁבַּתֶּֽהָ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Remembers Jerusalem [in the] days of her affliction and her wanderings all her precious things which were from days of antiquity, when fell her people into [the] hand of [a] foe and there was no helper for her; saw her foes, they laughed at her ceasing.

en.L: Jerusalem remembers, in the days of her affliction and her wandering, \q all her precious things that were from days of old; \q when her people fell into the hand of the foe, and there was no one to help her, \q the foes saw her; they laughed at her downfall.
en.B: In the days of her misery and homelessness Jerusalem remembers \q all the treasures that were hers in days gone by. \q When her people fell into the foe's hands and no one came to help her, \q her foes looked on and laughed at her ruin.
en.R: Now Jerusalem suffers and has no home, and she remembers \q all the good things she had long ago. \q Her people fell into the power of the enemy, and no one helped her. \q Her enemies saw her and laughed because she was ruined.

pt.L: Jerusalém se lembra, nos dias da sua aflição e da sua errância, \q de todas as suas coisas preciosas que existiam desde os dias antigos; \q quando o seu povo caiu na mão do adversário, e não havia quem a ajudasse, \q os adversários a viram; riram-se do seu fim.
pt.B: Nos dias da sua miséria e da sua vida sem lar, Jerusalém se lembra \q de todos os tesouros que eram seus em tempos passados. \q Quando o seu povo caiu nas mãos do adversário e ninguém veio ajudá-la, \q os seus adversários ficaram olhando e riram da sua ruína.
pt.R: Agora Jerusalém sofre e não tem casa, e ela se lembra \q de todas as coisas boas que tinha muito tempo atrás. \q O seu povo caiu nas mãos do inimigo, e ninguém a ajudou. \q Os seus inimigos a viram e riram porque ela estava arruinada.

es.L: Jerusalén se acuerda, en los días de su aflicción y de su andar errante, \q de todas sus cosas preciosas que tenía desde los días antiguos; \q cuando su pueblo cayó en mano del adversario y no hubo quien la ayudara, \q la vieron los adversarios; se rieron de su caída.
es.B: En los días de su miseria y de su vida sin hogar, Jerusalén recuerda \q todos los tesoros que fueron suyos en tiempos pasados. \q Cuando su pueblo cayó en manos del adversario y nadie vino a ayudarla, \q sus adversarios la miraron y se rieron de su ruina.
es.R: Ahora Jerusalén sufre y no tiene hogar, y se acuerda \q de todas las cosas buenas que tenía hace mucho tiempo. \q Su pueblo cayó en poder del enemigo, y nadie la ayudó. \q Sus enemigos la vieron y se rieron porque estaba arruinada.

vi.L: Giê-ru-sa-lem nhớ lại, trong những ngày khốn khổ và lưu lạc của nàng, \q mọi của quý của nàng đã có từ những ngày xưa; \q khi dân nàng sa vào tay kẻ địch, và không có ai giúp nàng, \q các kẻ địch đã thấy nàng; chúng cười nhạo sự sụp đổ của nàng.
vi.B: Trong những ngày khốn khổ và không nhà cửa, Giê-ru-sa-lem nhớ lại \q mọi báu vật nàng từng có trong những ngày xa xưa. \q Khi dân nàng sa vào tay quân địch mà chẳng ai đến cứu giúp, \q kẻ thù nhìn nàng và cười nhạo sự điêu tàn của nàng.
vi.R: Nay Giê-ru-sa-lem khốn khổ và không còn nhà, và nàng nhớ lại \q mọi điều tốt đẹp nàng đã có từ lâu xưa. \q Dân nàng rơi vào quyền lực của kẻ thù, và chẳng ai giúp nàng. \q Kẻ thù nhìn thấy nàng và cười nhạo vì nàng đã bị tàn phá.

fr.L: Jérusalem se souvient, aux jours de son affliction et de son errance, \q de tous ses trésors qui étaient [là] depuis les jours d’autrefois ; \q quand son peuple est tombé dans la main de l’adversaire, et qu’il n’y avait personne pour l’aider, \q les adversaires l’ont vue ; ils ont ri de sa chute.
fr.B: Aux jours de sa misère et de son errance, Jérusalem se souvient \q de tous les trésors qui étaient les siens aux jours anciens. \q Quand son peuple est tombé aux mains de l’adversaire, et que personne ne venait à son secours, \q ses adversaires l’ont regardée et ont ri de sa ruine.
fr.R: Maintenant Jérusalem souffre et n’a plus de maison, et elle se souvient \q de toutes les bonnes choses qu’elle avait autrefois. \q Son peuple est tombé au pouvoir de l’ennemi, et personne ne l’a aidée. \q Ses ennemis l’ont vue et se sont moqués d’elle parce qu’elle était ruinée.

sw.L: Yerusalemu anakumbuka, katika siku za mateso yake na kutangatanga kwake, \q vitu vyake vyote vya thamani vilivyokuwa tangu siku za kale; \q watu wake walipoanguka mkononi mwa mtesi, wala hapakuwa na wa kumsaidia, \q watesi walimwona; walicheka kuanguka kwake.
sw.B: Katika siku za taabu yake na za kukosa makao, Yerusalemu anakumbuka \q hazina zote alizokuwa nazo siku za zamani. \q Watu wake walipoanguka mikononi mwa mtesi, wala hakuna aliyekuja kumsaidia, \q watesi wake walimtazama na kuyacheka maangamizi yake.
sw.R: Sasa Yerusalemu anateseka wala hana makao, naye anakumbuka \q mambo yote mazuri aliyokuwa nayo zamani. \q Watu wake walianguka mikononi mwa adui, wala hakuna aliyemsaidia. \q Adui zake walimwona, wakacheka kwa sababu ameangamia.

ko.L: 예루살렘이 고난과 떠돌던 날들에 \q 옛날부터 있던 자기의 모든 귀한 것들을 기억한다. \q 그 성의 백성이 대적의 손에 넘어지고 그 성을 돕는 자가 없을 때에, \q 대적들이 그 성을 보고 그 성의 끝남을 비웃었다.
ko.B: 예루살렘은 비참하게 떠돌며 사는 날에 \q 지난날 자기가 누리던 온갖 보물을 기억한다. \q 그 백성이 대적의 손에 쓰러지고 아무도 돕는 이가 없을 때에, \q 대적들은 그 모습을 보고 그 성의 몰락을 비웃었다.
ko.R: 이제 예루살렘은 고통 속에서 집도 없이 떠돌며, \q 오래전에 가졌던 좋은 것들을 모두 떠올린다. \q 그 백성이 원수의 손에 넘어갔을 때, 아무도 도와주지 않았다. \q 원수들은 그 성을 보고 망했다고 비웃었다.

decisions.choice: a verse of four lines
decisions.reason: This verse has four lines where the others in the chapter have three. Some think one of the middle lines was added as an explanation, but the Hebrew text has all four, and they are kept.

decisions.choice: her wandering: her homelessness
decisions.reason: The word means restless wandering, the state of someone with no home (Isaiah 58:7; Lamentations 3:19). Jerusalem's people have been driven from their houses.

decisions.choice: her precious things: everything she treasured
decisions.reason: The word means things that are desired or loved. Here it covers all the city's good things, its wealth and its people, which she remembers in her loss (compare verses 10-11).

decisions.choice: her downfall: her coming to an end
decisions.reason: This word is found only here. It comes from the verb "to cease" or "to stop", the same root as the word for the Sabbath. The foes laugh because she is finished.

decisions.choice: Now Jerusalem suffers and has no home, and she remembers
decisions.reason: Readable turns the phrase "in the days of her affliction and her wandering" into its own clause.

source.text: חֵ֤טְא חָֽטְאָה֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם עַל־כֵּ֖ן לְנִידָ֣ה הָיָ֑תָה כָּֽל־מְכַבְּדֶ֤יהָ הִזִּיל֨וּהָ֙ כִּי־רָא֣וּ עֶרְוָתָ֔הּ גַּם־הִ֥יא נֶאֶנְחָ֖ה וַתָּ֥שָׁב אָחֽוֹר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Sin has sinned Jerusalem; therefore an impure thing she has become; all [who] honored her despise her, for they have seen her nakedness; also she groans and has turned backward.

en.L: Jerusalem has sinned a sin; therefore she has become an impure thing; \q all who honored her despise her, for they have seen her nakedness; \q she herself also groans and turns backward.
en.B: Jerusalem has sinned greatly, and so she has become unclean; \q all who honored her despise her, for they have seen her naked; \q she herself groans and turns her face away.
en.R: Jerusalem sinned terribly, so she became unclean. \q Those who used to respect her now look down on her, because they have seen her naked and ashamed. \q She groans and turns away.

pt.L: Jerusalém pecou um pecado; por isso se tornou uma coisa impura; \q todos os que a honravam a desprezam, porque viram a sua nudez; \q ela mesma também geme e volta para trás.
pt.B: Jerusalém pecou gravemente, e por isso ficou impura; \q todos os que a honravam a desprezam, pois a viram nua; \q ela mesma geme e desvia o rosto.
pt.R: Jerusalém pecou terrivelmente, por isso ficou impura. \q Os que antes a respeitavam agora a olham com desprezo, porque a viram nua e envergonhada. \q Ela geme e vira o rosto para o outro lado.

es.L: Jerusalén ha pecado gravemente; por eso ha llegado a ser cosa impura; \q todos los que la honraban la desprecian, porque han visto su desnudez; \q también ella gime y se vuelve atrás.
es.B: Jerusalén ha pecado gravemente, y por eso se ha vuelto impura; \q todos los que la honraban la desprecian, porque la han visto desnuda; \q ella misma gime y aparta la cara.
es.R: Jerusalén pecó terriblemente, y por eso quedó impura. \q Los que antes la respetaban ahora la miran con desprecio, porque la han visto desnuda y avergonzada. \q Ella gime y se da la vuelta.

vi.L: Giê-ru-sa-lem đã phạm một tội [nặng]; vì thế nàng đã trở thành một vật ô uế; \q mọi kẻ từng tôn trọng nàng đều khinh bỉ nàng, vì chúng đã thấy sự trần truồng của nàng; \q chính nàng cũng rên siết và quay lui.
vi.B: Giê-ru-sa-lem đã phạm tội trầm trọng, nên nàng trở thành ô uế; \q mọi kẻ từng kính trọng nàng nay khinh rẻ nàng, vì đã thấy nàng trần truồng; \q chính nàng cũng rên rỉ và quay mặt đi.
vi.R: Giê-ru-sa-lem đã phạm tội nặng nề, nên nàng trở thành ô uế. \q Những người từng kính trọng nàng nay coi thường nàng, vì họ đã thấy nàng trần truồng và nhục nhã. \q Nàng rên rỉ và quay đi.

fr.L: Jérusalem a péché un péché ; c’est pourquoi elle est devenue une chose impure ; \q tous ceux qui l’honoraient la méprisent, car ils ont vu sa nudité ; \q elle-même aussi gémit et se retourne en arrière.
fr.B: Jérusalem a gravement péché, et ainsi elle est devenue impure ; \q tous ceux qui l’honoraient la méprisent, car ils l’ont vue nue ; \q elle-même gémit et détourne le visage.
fr.R: Jérusalem a terriblement péché, alors elle est devenue impure. \q Ceux qui la respectaient la regardent maintenant de haut, parce qu’ils l’ont vue nue et couverte de honte. \q Elle gémit et se détourne.

sw.L: Yerusalemu ametenda dhambi [kubwa]; kwa hiyo amekuwa kitu najisi; \q wote waliomheshimu wanamdharau, kwa maana wameuona uchi wake; \q yeye mwenyewe pia anaugua na kugeuka nyuma.
sw.B: Yerusalemu ametenda dhambi kubwa, kwa hiyo amekuwa najisi; \q wote waliomheshimu wanamdharau, kwa maana wamemwona uchi; \q yeye mwenyewe anaugua na kugeuza uso wake.
sw.R: Yerusalemu alitenda dhambi mbaya sana, kwa hiyo akawa najisi. \q Wale waliokuwa wakimheshimu sasa wanamdharau, kwa sababu wamemwona akiwa uchi na mwenye aibu. \q Anaugua na kugeuka upande mwingine.

ko.L: 예루살렘이 죄를 짓고 또 지었다. 그러므로 그 성이 부정한 것이 되었다. \q 그 성을 존경하던 자들이 모두 그 성을 멸시한다. 그 성의 벌거벗음을 보았기 때문이다. \q 그 성도 탄식하며 뒤로 돌아선다.
ko.B: 예루살렘이 크게 죄를 지었다. 그래서 부정한 것이 되었다. \q 그 성을 우러러보던 이들이 모두 그 성을 업신여긴다. 그 벗은 몸을 보았기 때문이다. \q 그 성도 신음하며 얼굴을 돌린다.
ko.R: 예루살렘은 너무나 큰 죄를 지어서 부정하게 되었다. \q 그 성을 존경하던 사람들이 이제는 업신여긴다. 그 성이 벌거벗겨져 부끄러움을 당하는 것을 보았기 때문이다. \q 그 성은 신음하며 얼굴을 돌린다.

decisions.choice: has sinned a sin: has sinned greatly
decisions.reason: The noun and verb from the same root strengthen each other: her sin was grave. Verse 20 doubles a verb in the same way ("I have been very rebellious").

decisions.choice: an impure thing: something unclean that others keep away from
decisions.reason: The word is spelled with an extra letter compared with the word for impurity in verse 17 (niddah). It may be another spelling of that word, or it may come from a verb meaning to shake the head or to wander, giving "an object of scorn" or "a homeless wanderer". Her nakedness here and the uncleanness on her skirts in verse 9 favor impurity.

decisions.choice: impurity: the picture of a woman made unclean by her monthly bleeding
decisions.reason: Under the law, a woman's monthly bleeding made her ritually unclean and kept her apart from others for a time (Leviticus 15:19-24). Being unclean in this way was not a sin, but the prophets used it as a picture of defilement that makes others draw back (Ezekiel 36:17). Jerusalem is shunned like that.

decisions.choice: they have seen her nakedness: she is publicly shamed
decisions.reason: To be stripped and seen naked was the deepest disgrace. The prophets picture the punishment of a city that was unfaithful in this way (Isaiah 47:3; Ezekiel 16:37; Nahum 3:5).

decisions.choice: unclean (Balanced, Readable); turns her face away (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "unclean", the word used in the laws of purity. Balanced shows that she turns away in shame.

decisions.choice: naked and ashamed
decisions.reason: Readable adds "ashamed" to say what being seen naked meant (m4).

decisions.choice: impura
decisions.reason: "Impuro" is the word of the laws of purity in this translation's Old Testament ("puro, impuro"), so Balanced and Readable say "impura" where the English says "unclean"; "suja" would speak of dirt, not of ritual impurity (m3).

decisions.choice: "ha pecado gravemente"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the root for emphasis ("sinned a sin"); a word-for-word Spanish copy reads as an error, so even Literal gives its force with "gravemente".

source.text: טֻמְאָתָ֣הּ בְּשׁוּלֶ֗יהָ לֹ֤א זָֽכְרָה֙ אַחֲרִיתָ֔הּ וַתֵּ֣רֶד פְּלָאִ֔ים אֵ֥ין מְנַחֵ֖ם לָ֑הּ רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת־עָנְיִ֔י כִּ֥י הִגְדִּ֖יל אוֹיֵֽב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Her uncleanness [was] in her skirts; not she remembered her end; and she has come down wondrously; there is not a comforter for her. See, Yahweh, my affliction, for has magnified himself [the] enemy!

en.L: Her uncleanness [is] in her skirts; she did not remember her end; \q and she has come down astonishingly; she has no comforter. \q See, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my affliction, for the enemy has made himself great!
en.B: Her skirts are stained with her uncleanness; she gave no thought to where she was heading; \q her fall has been beyond belief, and there is no one to comfort her. \q Look, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, at my misery, for the enemy has triumphed!
en.R: Her clothes were stained with her uncleanness. She did not think about what would happen to her. \q Her fall was shocking, and no one comforts her. \q Zion cries: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, see how I suffer! My enemy has won!

pt.L: A sua impureza [está] nas suas saias; ela não se lembrou do seu fim; \q e desceu de modo espantoso; não tem quem a console. \q Vê, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, a minha aflição, pois o inimigo se engrandeceu!
pt.B: As suas saias estão manchadas com a sua impureza; ela não pensou no rumo que seguia; \q a sua queda foi inacreditável, e não há quem a console. \q Olha, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, para a minha miséria, pois o inimigo triunfou!
pt.R: As roupas dela estavam manchadas com a sua impureza. Ela não pensou no que ia acontecer com ela. \q A sua queda foi chocante, e ninguém a consola. \q Sião grita: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, vê como eu sofro! O meu inimigo venceu!

es.L: Su inmundicia [está] en sus faldas; no se acordó de su final; \q y ha descendido de modo asombroso; no tiene quien la consuele. \q Mira, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, mi aflicción, ¡porque el enemigo se ha engrandecido!
es.B: Sus faldas están manchadas de su impureza; no pensó adónde la llevaba su camino; \q su caída ha sido increíble, y no hay quien la consuele. \q ¡Mira, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, mi miseria, porque el enemigo ha triunfado!
es.R: Su ropa estaba manchada con su impureza. No pensó en lo que le iba a pasar. \q Su caída fue terrible, y nadie la consuela. \q Sion clama: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡mira cuánto sufro! ¡Mi enemigo ha ganado!

vi.L: Sự ô uế của nàng [ở] nơi vạt áo nàng; nàng đã không nhớ đến kết cuộc của mình; \q và nàng đã sa xuống cách lạ lùng; nàng không có người an ủi. \q Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin xem nỗi khốn khổ của tôi, vì kẻ thù đã tự tôn mình lên!
vi.B: Vạt áo nàng vấy bẩn sự ô uế; nàng chẳng hề nghĩ đến nơi mình sẽ đi tới; \q nàng sa sút đến mức không ai ngờ, chẳng có ai an ủi nàng. \q Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin đoái xem nỗi khốn khổ của tôi, vì kẻ thù đã đắc thắng!
vi.R: Quần áo nàng vấy bẩn vì sự ô uế. Nàng không nghĩ đến điều sẽ xảy đến cho mình. \q Nàng sa sút thật thảm hại, và không ai an ủi nàng. \q Si-ôn kêu lên: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin xem tôi khổ biết bao! Kẻ thù tôi đã thắng rồi!

fr.L: Son impureté [est] dans les pans de sa [robe] ; elle ne s’est pas souvenue de sa fin ; \q et elle est descendue de manière étonnante ; elle n’a pas de consolateur. \q Vois, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, mon affliction, car l’ennemi s’est fait grand !
fr.B: Les pans de sa robe sont souillés de son impureté ; elle n’a pas pensé à l’endroit où elle allait ; \q sa chute a été incroyable, et personne ne la console. \q Regarde, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ma misère, car l’ennemi triomphe !
fr.R: Ses vêtements étaient tachés par son impureté. Elle n’a pas pensé à ce qui allait lui arriver. \q Sa chute a été terrible, et personne ne la console. \q Sion s’écrie : {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, vois comme je souffre ! Mon ennemi a gagné !

sw.L: Uchafu wake [uko] katika pindo za nguo zake; hakukumbuka mwisho wake; \q naye ameshuka kwa namna ya kushangaza; hana mfariji. \q Ona, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mateso yangu, kwa maana adui amejikweza!
sw.B: Nguo zake zimetiwa doa la unajisi wake; hakufikiri anakoelekea; \q anguko lake limepita kiasi, wala hakuna wa kumfariji. \q Tazama, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, taabu yangu, kwa maana adui ameshinda!
sw.R: Nguo zake zilichafuliwa na unajisi wake. Hakufikiri kitakachompata. \q Anguko lake liliwashtua watu, wala hakuna anayemfariji. \q Sayuni analia: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ona jinsi ninavyoteseka! Adui yangu ameshinda!

ko.L: 그 성의 부정함이 그 옷자락에 [묻어] 있었다. 그 성은 자기의 끝을 생각하지 않았다. \q 그 성이 놀랍도록 낮아졌으나 위로하는 자가 없다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 저의 고난을 보십시오. 원수가 스스로 높아졌습니다!
ko.B: 그 성의 치맛자락에는 부정함이 묻어 있다. 그 성은 자기가 어디로 가는지 생각하지 않았다. \q 그 성이 믿을 수 없을 만큼 무너졌는데도 위로하는 이가 아무도 없다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 저의 비참함을 보십시오. 원수가 의기양양합니다!
ko.R: 그 성의 옷은 부정한 것으로 더러워졌다. 그 성은 앞으로 무슨 일이 닥칠지 생각하지 않았다. \q 그 성은 끔찍하게 무너졌고, 아무도 위로해 주지 않는다. \q 시온이 부르짖는다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 얼마나 고통당하는지 보십시오! 원수가 이겼습니다!

decisions.choice: her uncleanness in her skirts: a stain she cannot hide
decisions.reason: The picture goes on from verse 8: the blood of a woman's monthly bleeding has stained the hem of her dress, so her uncleanness is plain to everyone (Leviticus 15:19-24). It stands for Jerusalem's sin, now exposed to all.

decisions.choice: she did not remember her end: she gave no thought to where her way would lead
decisions.reason: Her "end" is what would come of her conduct. Moses said of Israel, "If they were wise, they would understand their end" (Deuteronomy 32:29), and Babylon is charged in the same words (Isaiah 47:7).

decisions.choice: See, LORD, my affliction: Zion speaks for the first time
decisions.reason: Up to here the poet has spoken about the city. Now, without any word to introduce her, Zion herself cries out to the LORD in the first person ("my affliction"). The poet's voice returns in verses 10-11, and from verse 11c Zion speaks to the end of the chapter, apart from verse 17. Her words are not set off as a quotation.

decisions.choice: the enemy has made himself great: he boasts in his victory
decisions.reason: The verb means to make oneself great, to act with arrogance over a fallen enemy (Psalm 35:26; Jeremiah 48:26).

decisions.choice: Zion cries:
decisions.reason: Readable says who is now speaking, since the Hebrew changes voice without warning (m3).

decisions.choice: Vê, SENHOR (L); Olha, SENHOR (B); tu to God
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Zion and the poet speak to God with "tu" at every level (docs/portuguese-style.md section 4), so the imperatives are "vê", "olha", "lembra-te". God's name as a vocative has no article, "SENHOR" in capitals, inside the divine_name span.

decisions.choice: vocative "SEÑOR" with no "oh"
decisions.reason: As in the Spanish Psalms and prophets, the LORD addressed directly takes no "oh". Zion's words take no quotation marks; Readable marks the change of speaker with "Sion clama:", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: When Zion speaks (1:9c, 11c–22; 2:20–22) she says "tôi", and calls on God with "Lạy CHÚA", with no quotation marks
decisions.reason: Zion speaks as the wounded city, not as a worshipper in a prayer form; "tôi" keeps one voice through her complaints to God and to the passers-by. The poet's and Zion's words take no quotation marks, as the English; Readable's "Si-ôn kêu lên:" introduces her as the English Readable does. Recorded once for the book.

decisions.choice: Zion’s words without quotation marks, with feminine agreement ("je suis devenue", "m’a traitée"), for the whole book; Readable "Sion s’écrie :" as the English Readable
decisions.reason: As the English: the poet, Zion and the man of chapter 3 speak in turn without quotation marks, and a decision marks each change of speaker. French agreement in the feminine makes plain that Zion is speaking.

decisions.choice: "Ona, BWANA, mateso yangu" with no speaker named and no quotation marks
decisions.reason: Here Zion speaks for the first time. Hebrew shows the speaker is feminine in its verbs and pronouns; Swahili verbs and pronouns show no gender, so the change of voice rests on "yangu" after the poet's "yake". Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew's sudden turn without adding words, and, as for all the voices of the book, use no quotation marks; Readable names the speaker, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Zion speaks to God in 합쇼체 with "저" and the vocative "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여"; to passers-by and peoples in plain 해라체 with "나"
decisions.reason: Korean must mark whom Zion is speaking to. Turning to God (1:9c, 11c, 20-22) she prays in the formal polite style, as Korean prayers do in the Psalms and Jeremiah; to the people on the road (1:12-16, 18-19) she speaks in the plain style. The poet narrates in the plain written style and gives God the honorific. No quotation marks, as in the English.

source.text: יָדוֹ֙ פָּ֣רַשׂ צָ֔ר עַ֖ל כָּל־מַחֲמַדֶּ֑יהָ כִּֽי־רָאֲתָ֤ה גוֹיִם֙ בָּ֣אוּ מִקְדָּשָׁ֔הּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּ֔יתָה לֹא־יָבֹ֥אוּ בַקָּהָ֖ל לָֽךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: His hand has spread out [the] foe over all her desirable things; for she has seen nations, they have entered her sanctuary, whom you commanded [that] not they should enter into [the] assembly of yours.

en.L: The foe has spread out his hand over all her precious things; \q for she has seen nations enter her sanctuary, \q [those] whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded [that] they should not enter into {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} assembly.
en.B: The foe has reached out his hand for all her treasures; \q she has watched the nations enter her sanctuary, \q the very ones {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forbade to enter {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} assembly.
en.R: The enemy has grabbed all her treasures. \q She watched foreign nations go into her temple, \q though {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, had commanded that such people must never join {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people when they gather.

pt.L: O adversário estendeu a sua mão sobre todas as suas coisas preciosas; \q pois ela viu nações entrarem no seu santuário, \q [aquelas] a quem {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ordenaste [que] não entrassem na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} assembleia.
pt.B: O adversário estendeu a mão sobre todos os seus tesouros; \q ela viu as nações entrarem no seu santuário, \q justamente aquelas que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} proibiste de entrar na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} assembleia.
pt.R: O inimigo agarrou todos os tesouros dela. \q Ela viu nações estrangeiras entrarem no seu templo, \q embora {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, tivesses ordenado que essa gente nunca se juntasse ao {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} povo quando ele se reúne.

es.L: El adversario ha extendido su mano sobre todas sus cosas preciosas; \q porque ella ha visto a las naciones entrar en su santuario, \q [aquellas] a las que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} ordenaste que no entraran en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} asamblea.
es.B: El adversario ha puesto la mano sobre todos sus tesoros; \q ella ha visto a las naciones entrar en su santuario, \q las mismas a las que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} prohibiste entrar en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} asamblea.
es.R: El enemigo se ha apoderado de todos sus tesoros. \q Ella vio a pueblos extranjeros entrar en su templo, \q aunque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, habías ordenado que esa gente nunca se uniera a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo cuando se reúne.

vi.L: Kẻ địch đã giương tay ra trên mọi của quý của nàng; \q vì nàng đã thấy các dân tộc vào nơi thánh của nàng, \q [những kẻ] mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã truyền rằng chúng không được vào hội chúng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Kẻ thù đã vươn tay chiếm đoạt mọi báu vật của nàng; \q nàng đã phải nhìn các dân ngoại tiến vào nơi thánh của mình, \q chính những kẻ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã cấm không được vào hội chúng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Kẻ thù đã cướp hết mọi báu vật của nàng. \q Nàng đã thấy các dân ngoại đi vào đền thờ của nàng, \q dù {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, đã truyền rằng những người như thế không bao giờ được nhập vào dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} khi họ nhóm họp.

fr.L: L’adversaire a étendu sa main sur tous ses trésors ; \q car elle a vu des nations entrer dans son sanctuaire, \q [celles] à qui {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} avais ordonné qu’elles n’entrent pas dans {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} assemblée.
fr.B: L’adversaire a porté la main sur tous ses trésors ; \q elle a vu les nations entrer dans son sanctuaire, \q celles-là mêmes à qui {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} avais interdit d’entrer dans {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} assemblée.
fr.R: L’ennemi s’est emparé de tous ses trésors. \q Elle a vu des nations étrangères entrer dans son temple, \q alors que {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} avais ordonné que ces gens-là ne se joignent jamais à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple quand il se rassemble.

sw.L: Mtesi amenyosha mkono wake juu ya vitu vyake vyote vya thamani; \q kwa maana ameona mataifa yakiingia patakatifu pake, \q [wale] ambao uliamuru wasiingie katika kusanyiko {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}.
sw.B: Mtesi amenyosha mkono wake kunyakua hazina zake zote; \q ameyaona mataifa yakiingia mahali pake patakatifu, \q yale yale uliyoyakataza yasiingie katika kusanyiko {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}.
sw.R: Adui amenyakua hazina zake zote. \q Aliyaona mataifa ya kigeni yakiingia hekaluni mwake, \q ingawa {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uliamuru kwamba watu kama hao wasijiunge kamwe na watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wanapokusanyika.

ko.L: 대적이 그 성의 모든 귀한 것들 위에 자기 손을 폈다. \q 그 성은 민족들이 자기 성소에 들어가는 것을 보았다. \q 주님께서 주님의 회중에 들어오지 못하게 명령하신 자들이다.
ko.B: 대적이 그 성의 모든 보물에 손을 뻗쳤다. \q 그 성은 이방 민족들이 성소에 들어가는 것을 지켜보았다. \q 주님께서 주님의 회중에 들어오지 못하게 하신 바로 그 민족들이었다.
ko.R: 원수가 그 성의 보물을 모두 움켜쥐었다. \q 그 성은 이방 민족들이 성전에 들어가는 것을 지켜보았다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서는 그런 사람들이 주님의 백성의 모임에 절대로 함께하지 못하게 명령하셨습니다.

decisions.choice: her precious things: the treasures of the temple and the city
decisions.reason: The Babylonians carried off the gold, silver and bronze of the LORD's house and the wealth of the palace (2 Kings 24:13; 25:13-17).

decisions.choice: nations whom you commanded not to enter your assembly
decisions.reason: The law kept certain foreign peoples out of "the assembly of the LORD" (Deuteronomy 23:4). Now foreigners have gone further than the assembly: they have walked into the holy place itself, as conquerors.

decisions.choice: you, your: the poet turns to speak to God
decisions.reason: In the middle of describing Zion, the poet addresses God directly: "you commanded". The last word, "your", has an ending that can be read as addressing Zion ("your assembly", hers), but at the end of a verse the same form is used in speaking to a man, and the commandment and the assembly are the LORD's (Deuteronomy 23:4).

decisions.choice: you, LORD ... join your people when they gather
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD, whom the poet now addresses (m3), and explains the assembly as the gathering of God's people for worship.

decisions.choice: "주님" for "you" when the poet turns to God
decisions.reason: Korean does not address God with a second-person pronoun; "주님께서" and "주님의" stand for "you" and "your". Readable, which names the LORD here as the English does, ends in 합쇼체 because the poet is speaking to God.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives ("kusanyiko lako|Lako"), none on verb prefixes ("uliamuru")
alternatives: a span wherever the English has one
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb, and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the Swahili of Lamentations has fewer deity_pronoun spans than the English: they stand only on free pronouns and possessives that refer to God ("wewe", "yako", "lake", "hasira yake"). Mid-sentence, every free pronoun or possessive that means God takes the span, including "nami", "naye", "yeye" and "kwangu"; a word that opens a sentence is written plainly with its capital, and "naye" followed by a noun ("naye BWANA") is a conjunction with no span.

source.text: כָּל־עַמָּ֤הּ נֶאֱנָחִים֙ מְבַקְּשִׁ֣ים לֶ֔חֶם נָתְנ֧וּ מַחֲמַדֵּיהֶ֛םבְּאֹ֖כֶל לְהָשִׁ֣יב נָ֑פֶשׁ רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטָה כִּ֥י הָיִ֖יתִי זוֹלֵלָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: All her people [are] groaning, seeking bread; they have given their desirable things for food to bring back life. See, Yahweh, and look, for I have become worthless.

en.L: All her people groan, seeking bread; \q they have given their precious things for food, to bring back life. \q See, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and look, for I have become worthless.
en.B: All her people groan as they search for bread; \q they trade their treasures for food to stay alive. \q Look, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and take notice, for I am treated as worthless.
en.R: All her people groan as they look for bread. \q They give away their treasures for food so that they can stay alive. \q Zion cries: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, look at me! See how people despise me!

pt.L: Todo o seu povo geme, buscando pão; \q deram as suas coisas preciosas por comida, para fazer voltar a vida. \q Vê, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, e olha, porque me tornei desprezível.
pt.B: Todo o seu povo geme enquanto procura pão; \q trocam os seus tesouros por comida para continuar vivos. \q Olha, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, e repara, pois sou tratada como coisa sem valor.
pt.R: Todo o povo dela geme enquanto procura pão. \q Eles dão os seus tesouros em troca de comida para poderem continuar vivos. \q Sião grita: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, olha para mim! Vê como as pessoas me desprezam!

es.L: Todo su pueblo gime buscando pan; \q han dado sus cosas preciosas por comida para hacer volver la vida. \q Mira, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y observa, porque he quedado despreciada.
es.B: Todo su pueblo gime mientras busca pan; \q cambian sus tesoros por comida para seguir con vida. \q Mira, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y fíjate, porque me tratan como si no valiera nada.
es.R: Todo su pueblo gime mientras busca pan. \q Dan sus tesoros a cambio de comida para poder seguir vivos. \q Sion clama: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡mírame! ¡Mira cómo me desprecian!

vi.L: Cả dân nàng đều rên siết, tìm bánh; \q họ đã đổi những của quý của mình lấy đồ ăn để hồi lại sự sống. \q Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin xem và nhìn, vì tôi đã trở nên đáng khinh.
vi.B: Cả dân nàng rên rỉ đi tìm bánh ăn; \q họ đổi báu vật lấy thức ăn để giữ mạng sống. \q Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin nhìn xem và để ý, vì tôi bị coi như đồ bỏ đi.
vi.R: Cả dân nàng rên rỉ khi đi tìm bánh. \q Họ đem báu vật đổi lấy thức ăn để được sống còn. \q Si-ôn kêu lên: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin nhìn tôi! Xin xem người ta khinh bỉ tôi thế nào!

fr.L: Tout son peuple gémit, cherchant du pain ; \q ils ont donné leurs trésors pour de la nourriture, pour ramener la vie. \q Vois, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et regarde, car je suis devenue méprisable.
fr.B: Tout son peuple gémit en cherchant du pain ; \q ils échangent leurs trésors contre de la nourriture pour rester en vie. \q Regarde, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et vois : on me traite comme une chose sans valeur.
fr.R: Tout son peuple gémit en cherchant du pain. \q Les gens donnent leurs trésors pour avoir à manger et rester en vie. \q Sion s’écrie : {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, regarde-moi ! Vois comme les gens me méprisent !

sw.L: Watu wake wote wanaugua, wakitafuta mkate; \q wametoa vitu vyao vya thamani kwa chakula, ili kurudisha uhai. \q Ona, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, na utazame, kwa maana nimekuwa duni.
sw.B: Watu wake wote wanaugua wakitafuta mkate; \q wanabadilisha hazina zao kwa chakula ili waendelee kuishi. \q Tazama, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uangalie, kwa maana ninahesabiwa kuwa si kitu.
sw.R: Watu wake wote wanaugua wanapotafuta mkate. \q Wanatoa hazina zao ili wapate chakula na kubaki hai. \q Sayuni analia: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, niangalie! Ona jinsi watu wanavyonidharau!

ko.L: 그 성의 모든 백성이 탄식하며 빵을 구한다. \q 목숨을 되돌리려고 그들의 귀한 것들을 먹을 것과 바꾸었다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 보시고 살펴보십시오. 제가 천하게 되었습니다.
ko.B: 그 백성은 모두 탄식하며 빵을 찾아 헤맨다. \q 살아남으려고 보물을 내주고 먹을 것을 얻는다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 보시고 살펴 주십시오. 제가 이렇게 멸시를 당합니다.
